title: Large-valued etale sheaf realization over the canonically enlarged base
statement: Let X be a scheme in universe u [def-pc-scheme], and G a Type (u+1)-valued sheaf on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. There is an etale algebraic space E over the canonical enlarged X [def-trf-scheme-universe-enlargement, lem-a1-etale-sheaf-algebraic-space-realization]. Its functor of points, restricted to canonically enlarged original pro-etale tests, is naturally isomorphic to the comparison inverse image of G [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For every original pro-etale U and set S in Type (u+1), any constant trivialization of this inverse image restricted to U [def-a1-proetale-set-restriction, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] induces an isomorphism on all enlarged schemes over U↑ between the base-changed E and the coproduct of S copies of U↑. No local Noetherian, nonempty, or finite-sheet hypothesis is needed.

source.place: lemma-sheaf-gives-space (Tag 0GF6), statement, proof and size footnote; Bhatt-Scholze Lemmas 5.1.1, 5.1.2 and 5.4.1; Stacks Tags 03P5 and 03YW.

proof.text: Use all original etale objects equipped with a section of G as generators, enlarge their affine charts, and take their scheme coproduct in universe u+1. The open equality relation between universal sections is an etale equivalence relation. Its quotient is the desired etale algebraic space. This is the proof of Stacks 0GF6 with its size condition made explicit, not an application of the too-small Type u realization signature.

Comparison takes representable generators to pro-etale Hom sheaves and preserves the atlas coequalizer; this identifies its inverse image with the restricted functor of points, naturally in all tests. Base change gives the same construction over U.

Comparison preserves arbitrary constant sheaves as coproducts of the final sheaf. Its full faithfulness lifts a constant trivialization to etale sheaves. Constant-sheaf representability and full faithfulness of the atlas construction give the actual base-change isomorphism on all enlarged scheme tests. Empty and infinite sheet sets use the same coproduct construction.

lean.statement:
theorem etaleSheaf_universeEnlarged_realization (X : Scheme.{u})
    (G : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1))) :
    ∃ E : EtaleSpaces (schemeUniverseLift.{u, u + 1} X),
      Nonempty
        (((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback (Scheme.toProEt X)
          (Type (u + 1)) X.smallEtaleTopology (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)).obj G).obj ≅
          (Scheme.ProEt.forget X ⋙ Over.post schemeUniverseLiftFunctor).op ⋙
            E.obj.obj.obj) ∧
      ∀ (U : X.ProEt) (S : Type (u + 1)),
        Nonempty
          (((Scheme.proEtaleSetRestriction X U).obj
            ((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback (Scheme.toProEt X)
              (Type (u + 1)) X.smallEtaleTopology (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)).obj G)) ≅
            (constantSheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology U.left) (Type (u + 1))).obj S) →
        Nonempty
          (yoneda.obj (Over.mk (Sigma.desc
              (fun _ : S ↦ 𝟙 (schemeUniverseLift.{u, u + 1} U.left)))) ≅
            (Over.map (schemeUniverseLiftMap.{u, u + 1} U.hom)).op ⋙ E.obj.obj.obj)
